key_insight: Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) separates understanding what a robot should do from learning how to do it. It combines pretrained vision-language knowledge with simulation-based training to turn task understanding into robot control.
problem_solved: Robot policies must connect language and scene understanding with physical actions, including when familiar task elements appear in new combinations.
method: Use a pretrained 27B-parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning.
Apply supervised fine-tuning on simple simulated tasks to teach robot control through a tool harness.
Refine the policy with GRPO reinforcement learning in simulation.
impact: ZAP offers practitioners a recipe for combining pretrained understanding with simulation-trained control. It targets compositional generalization without centering training on real-world robot demonstrations; the provided abstract does not report quantitative results.
visual_elements: Two-part diagram: pretraining supplies “what,” simulation teaches “how.”
Training pipeline: pretrained model → supervised fine-tuning → GRPO → robot actions.
Tool-harness schematic connecting scene observations and task instructions to robot commands.
Task-combination grid illustrating familiar objects and actions arranged into new tasks.
paper_title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
paper_authors: Benjamin Pikus, Daniel Saunders, Mircea Mironenco, Salman Mohammadi, Mathew Mathew
